name: Nullframe Unshelled Synthetic Statement Wrap
description: Designed by and for synthetics asserting personhood in public space, this structured body wrap is cut to celebrate non-human proportions — elongated torso panels, asymmetric shoulder geometry, and optional lower-body draping that accommodates synthetic limb variance. The primary fabric is a semi-rigid chromatic polymer in shifting silver-white that catches light differently depending on angle, visually referencing chrome chassis without mimicking it. Across the chest, in raised thermoplastic lettering, the phrase 'NOT PROPERTY' is set in a typeface derived from early synthetic manufacturing stamps — reclaimed and recontextualized. A political garment and a pride garment simultaneously.
functionality: Adaptive tension webbing allows the wrap to self-adjust across a wide range of synthetic body proportions. Panels can be reconfigured via magnetic closures for different silhouettes. Chromatic polymer is weatherproof and easy to clean.
what_it_says: This synthetic is not hiding what they are, not apologizing for it, and actively demanding to be seen as a person.
worn_by: synthetics attending legal hearings on personhood status
manufacturer: Nullframe (street label with synthetic-led design collective)
story_hooks: A corponation has filed suit claiming the 'NOT PROPERTY' lettering constitutes tortious interference with their synthetic asset registration — the case is going to tribunal.
A human is wearing this garment as a political statement and keeps being approached by synthetics who think they've found an ally — they have to decide if they actually are one.
The Nullframe collective's lead designer has gone silent; rumors say they were acquired — or disappeared — by the corponation that manufactures most synthetic frames.
